---
title: "PCA in High Dimensions"
description: "Original mathematical teaching with a worked delivery-operations example; MML §10.5."
---

**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §10.5. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

Text, image and engineered feature vectors can have far more columns than observations. It is then useful to work with the smaller Gram matrix or use iterative methods.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
X_cX_c^\top\in\mathbb R^{N\times N},\quad X_c^\top X_c\in\mathbb R^{D\times D},\quad \operatorname{rank}(X_c)\leq\min(N-1,D)
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

If a dataset contains N=100 observations but D=10,000 features, the centered data rank is at most 99. A 100-by-100 Gram matrix can reveal nonzero singular-value information more economically than an explicit 10,000-by-10,000 covariance matrix.

## Why the mathematics matters

Do not reconstruct full high-dimensional eigenvectors from a zero singular value by dividing by it. Randomised SVD and iterative eigensolvers are practical for large sparse data.

## Explain or calculate

Why is a centered 100-row dataset unable to have 100 nonzero independent principal directions?
